title: Universal Planckian dissipation in the strange metal state of the cuprates
abstract:
Nature Communications, Published online: 26 July 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-75673-7

Through an analysis of existing data, the authors show that the “Planckian” relaxation rate in cuprate superconductors is doping independent. This follows from the finding that the square optical plasma frequency scales linearly with doping, which they further argue is a natural consequence of Mott physics.

title: Scaling and Population Loss in Mexican Urban Centres
abstract:
Nature Communications, Published online: 25 July 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-75780-5

We analysed urban growth dynamics in 69 Mexican metropolitan areas from 1990 to 2020 using radial scaling analysis. In 30 years, the urban population shifted outwards, with all central zones losing 2.5 million people, absorbed by the peripheries.

title: Finding the perfect promoter for Cas9 in homing gene drives using single cell transcriptome data
abstract:
Nature Communications, Published online: 25 July 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-76107-0

CRISPR homing gene drives can help control disease vectors but require precise Cas9 expression. Here, the drive performance of 35 Cas9 constructs with different promoters in Drosophila were compared to single cell RNA expression patterns of promoter-associated genes.

title: Scalable high resolution ancestry deconvolution for genomic data
abstract:
Nature Communications, Published online: 25 July 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-75391-0

The authors present Gnomix, a local ancestry framework that delivers leading accuracy across diverse admixed datasets on both whole-genome and array data with high efficiency, together with Gnofix, its fast phasing-error correction counterpart.

title: Electrically driven inverse metamagnetic transition in Sm1-xSrxMnO₃
abstract:
Nature Communications, Published online: 25 July 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-75886-w

Correlated oxides are known to exhibit metamagnetic switching from a non-ferromagnetic to ferromagnetic phase. Here, the authors demonstrate an electrically driven inverse-metamagnetic transition from a ferromagnetic state to an antiferromagnetic-like phase in an epitaxial Sm1-xSrxMnO3 thin film.

title: Retarding moisture-induced chemical degradation of Yttrium Tellurides by tailoring grain boundary chemistry
abstract:
Nature Communications, Published online: 25 July 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-76056-8

Y2Te3 thermoelectrics degrade in moist air as water molecules enter along grain boundaries. The authors show that 1 at.% Bi segregates to these boundaries, suppressing moisture ingress and preventing chemical degradation while preserving performance.

title: DICER1-related tumour predisposition mutations increase 3p-miRNA function and HERVH activity
abstract:
Nature Communications, Published online: 25 July 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-76094-2

DICER1 is often mutated in cancer, including in DICER1-related tumour predisposition. Here, the authors show that cancer-associated DICER1 mutations shift microRNA processing and reactivate HERVH endogenous retroviruses.

title: Neural dynamics for working memory and evidence integration during olfactory navigation in Drosophila
abstract:
Nature Communications, Published online: 25 July 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-75945-2

The authors describe a population of neurons in the navigation center of Drosophila that exhibits a persistent goal signal during olfactory navigation.
